sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Compiler settings for the client library
sections.what: Sets where the source is read, where type files are written, and that only type files are produced. It also sets which browser and modern library types are available.
sections.why: The client library is used by other packages through its types and must compile under the shared rules.
sections.watch_out: Keep rootDir and outDir consistent with the root project references, or the build will not find its outputs.

summary: Compiler settings for the React API client library. It checks the library and writes only type description files into dist.
purpose: Lets the build check the client library and produce the type information other packages use.
why: Likely reason: the client is consumed for its types, so only declaration files are needed here. The code does not state this directly.
how: Inherits the shared rules from the base config, turns on project references and declaration maps, reads source from src, writes declarations to dist, includes only src, and allows browser and modern JavaScript library types.
inputs: Source files in src, and the shared base config at tsconfig.base.json in the repo root.
outputs: Declaration files and their maps in dist. Type errors are printed when the check fails.
risks: Changing rootDir or outDir can break the root project references. Declaration-only output means the library is not runnable on its own, so another step must bundle it.
debug: If the build fails, run the root typecheck:libs command to see the error in context. If files are not found, check include and rootDir. If dist is empty, check that emitDeclarationOnly is still intended.
